toc.title: Pattern Chooser: Symptom to Best Answer
Names and Values to Know Exactly
Distractor Patterns and the Rule That Beats Them

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MCP: Model Context Protocol; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; SLA: service level agreement; CLI: command-line interface

  • A symptom-to-fix chooser for every domain
  • The exact names, flags and values that questions use
  • The distractor patterns and the rule that defeats each

2Pattern Chooser: Symptom to Best Answer

Domain 1: Agentic Architecture and Orchestration (27%)

If the problem is... The best answer is... Module
Loop never ends / ends too soon Stop on end_turn, continue on tool_use; no text parsing, no iteration cap as main stop 1
A mandatory step is skipped (verify before refund) Programmatic prerequisite gate or hook 3
A business limit must always hold Interception hook that blocks and redirects 3
Tool results come in mixed formats PostToolUse normalization hook 3
Escalation arrives without context Structured handoff summary 3
Report misses a whole area, subagents "succeeded" Fix the coordinator's decomposition 2
Subagent output lacks sources Pass findings + metadata in the prompt 2
Independent searches are slow Several Task calls in one response 2
12-file review is uneven and contradictory Per-file passes + integration pass 4
Unfamiliar legacy task Dynamic decomposition: map, prioritize, adapt 4
Resume after files changed Resume + tell it which files changed; stale → fresh summary 4
Compare two approaches from one analysis fork_session 4

Domain 2: Tool Design and MCP Integration (18%)

If the problem is... The best answer is... Module
Wrong tool among similar ones Richer descriptions (formats, examples, edge cases, boundaries) first 5
Two tools overlap Rename + rewrite, or split into purpose-specific tools 5
Agent cannot tell failure types Structured errors: category, isRetryable, message 5
Timeout vs no results confused Failure = error; no matches = valid empty success 5
Agent has 18 tools and misuses them Scope tools to roles (4 to 5) 6
Frequent small need in another role Scoped cross-role tool (verify_fact) 6
Must call a tool, any one tool_choice: "any" 6
A given tool must run first Forced tool selection 6
Share a server with the team Project .mcp.json + ${ENV} 6
Personal experimental server User ~/.claude.json 6
Search content / find files / edit unique text Grep / Glob / Edit; no unique anchor → Read + Write 6

Domain 3: Claude Code Configuration and Workflows (20%)

If the problem is... The best answer is... Module
Teammate misses standards Move from user to project CLAUDE.md 7
Huge CLAUDE.md .claude/rules/ files, @import 7
What did it load? /memory 7
Shared command .claude/commands/ 7
Verbose skill output context: fork 7
Ask for parameters argument-hint 7
Conventions by file type, spread out .claude/rules/ with paths: globs 7
Big multi-file change Plan mode, then execute 8
Small, clear fix Direct execution 8
Prose misunderstood 2 to 3 examples; tests first; interview pattern 8
CI hangs -p 8
CI needs machine-readable output --output-format json + --json-schema 8
Duplicate review comments Pass prior findings 8
Self-review finds nothing Independent instance 8, 11

Domain 4: Prompt Engineering and Structured Output (20%)

If the problem is... The best answer is... Module
Too many false positives Explicit report/skip criteria (not "be conservative"); disable noisy category meanwhile 9
Inconsistent severity Severity levels with code examples 9
Inconsistent format / ambiguous cases 2 to 4 few-shot examples with reasoning 9
Broken JSON Tool use + JSON schema 10
Fabricated values Nullable/optional fields 10
New categories appear Enum + other + detail; unclear 10
Totals do not add up Validation; calculated_total vs stated_total 10
Validation failed Retry with document + failure + errors; none if the info is absent 10
Cheap nightly job Batch API (50%, up to 24 h, custom_id); never for blocking work 11
SLA planning Interval + 24 h ≤ SLA 11

Domain 5: Context Management and Reliability (15%)

If the problem is... The best answer is... Module
Amounts/dates vanish in long chats Case-facts block outside summaries 12
Findings in the middle are missed Key summary first, section headers 12
Tool output bloat Trim to relevant fields 12
"Typical patterns" in long exploration Scratchpad, subagents, manifest, /compact 12
Wrong escalations Explicit criteria + few-shot; not sentiment or confidence 13
Customer asks for a person Escalate now 13
Several matches Ask for another identifier 13
Subagent failure Structured error context, partial results, coverage annotations 13
97% accuracy overall Per-type, per-field accuracy; stratified sampling; calibrated confidence 14
Conflicting statistics Both values, with sources and dates 14
Exam tip

Read the last sentence of the stem first, name the symptom, then match it to a row of this chooser.

3Names and Values to Know Exactly

Item Value
Loop signals stop_reason: tool_use (continue), end_turn (stop)
tool_choice "auto", "any", {"type":"tool","name":"..."}
Spawning Task tool (now Agent); allowedTools includes it; AgentDefinition
Hooks PostToolUse (results), call interception (PreToolUse in current docs)
MCP isError; .mcp.json (project) and ~/.claude.json (user); ${GITHUB_TOKEN}
Built-ins Read · Write · Edit · Bash · Grep · Glob
CLAUDE.md ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md · CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md · subdirectory files · .claude/rules/ · @import · /memory
Commands/skills .claude/commands/ · ~/.claude/commands/ · .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md · context: fork · allowed-tools · argument-hint
Rule frontmatter paths: with globs (**/*.test.tsx, terraform/**/*)
CLI -p/--print · --output-format json · --json-schema · --resume <name> · --fork-session
Batches 50% · up to 24 h · custom_id · no multi-turn tool calling
Error metadata errorCategory (transient/validation/permission/business) · isRetryable
Self-check fields calculated_total, stated_total, conflict_detected, detected_pattern
Exam 60 items · 120 min · 720/1,000 · 4 of 6 scenarios
Exam tip

Exact names matter: stop_reason, tool_choice, .mcp.json, context: fork, paths:, -p, --json-schema.

4Distractor Patterns and the Rule That Beats Them

Distractor Why it is wrong Rule
"Strengthen the prompt" for a hard requirement Probabilistic 1
"Add a classifier / routing layer" first Over-engineered before simple fixes 3
"Self-reported confidence" or "sentiment" as the trigger Poor proxies 6
"Blame the downstream agent" Logs point upstream 2
"Give every agent all tools" No least privilege 4
"Generic error message / empty success" Hides recovery information 5, 9
"Abort the whole run" Wastes partial results 9
"Use the bigger context window" Attention quality is the issue 7
"Batch for everything (50% off)" No latency guarantee 8
"Same session reviews itself" Keeps its reasoning 7
"Read everything up front" Burns context 10
Exam tip

A distractor is wrong because it is probabilistic, over-engineered, hiding information, over-privileged or mistimed.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Order of study D1 first (27%), then D3 and D4 (20% each), D2 (18%), D5 (15%)
Core stance Deterministic · root-cause · proportionate · least privilege · structured · independent · latency-matched · no silent failure · context-aware
Day before Reread this module and the ten rules in Module 0
